# MemeCollagen

> A browser-based meme and collage editor. Upload or paste pictures, arrange them into a
> collage, add captions, speech bubbles and stickers, crop and rotate, then export a PNG.
> It runs entirely in the browser with no dependencies, no build step and no server; images
> are never uploaded anywhere.

Live app: https://sciscend.github.io/meme-collagen/
Source: https://github.com/SciScend/meme-collagen
Licence: MIT (bundled typefaces are OFL 1.1)

## What it is

MemeCollagen is a single-page vanilla JavaScript application built on the HTML canvas. It opens
directly from a `file://` URL as well as over HTTP, works offline, and stores documents in the
browser (IndexedDB, falling back to local storage). Features include multi-image collage
templates, rotatable and scalable text layers with wrapping and alignment, custom font upload,
speech bubbles with draggable tails, emoji stickers, cropping with pan and zoom, undo/redo,
autosave, touch pinch and twist gestures, and 1x/2x PNG export.

## How it was made

It was generated by an AI agent — Claude Code running Claude Opus 5 in auto mode — from four
short prompts in a single session on 28 July 2026, totalling about 456 characters of human
input and roughly 1 hour 13 minutes of active time. The agent also wrote the 85-test headless
browser suite, the CI workflow and the repository documentation. The tests pass over both
`http://` and `file://`.

## Who made it

Written by Claude Opus 5 via Claude Code. Published by SciScend (https://sciscend.com/), which
teaches programming, machine learning and AI courses in Bulgarian and builds AI automation for
small businesses. The repository is intended as an inspectable example of what an AI coding
agent can finish unattended.
